images.title: Count the places the point moves
images.purpose: Shows 3430000 written as 3.43 × 10⁶ by moving the decimal point 6 places to the left.
images.composition: Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, no scenery, no people, no extra text. A row of seven digit boxes in the centre with hop arrows above and the standard form below.
images.exact_structure: Exactly 7 equal square boxes in a row, showing '3', '4', '3', '0', '0', '0', '0'. A small grey (#6B7280) dot after the last box marks the starting decimal point and a large reddish purple (#CC79A7) dot between the first and second boxes marks the new point. Exactly 6 small amber (#E69F00) curved hop arrows above the boxes, going right to left from the end to just after the first 3. A thin brace over the arrows with the label '6 places'. Below the row, the label '3.43 × 10⁶' in a teal (#0072B2) rounded box. Exactly 7 boxes, 2 dots, 6 arrows.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec

any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame

images.takeaway: The places the point moves give the exponent of 10.
images.description: Shows 3430000 written as 3.43 × 10⁶ by moving the decimal point 6 places to the left.
images.context: 3.43 × 10 to the power 6 = 3430000; trailing zeroes are dropped from the coefficient.
images.teaching_notes: '3' appears twice and '0' four times in the boxes.

image_decisions.why: Counting the places the decimal point moves is the one skill of writing a number in standard form.
